An object moving along a curve in the $x y$-plane has position $(x(t)\, y(t))$ at time $t >= 0$ with $frac(d x,d t)= 3 + cos lr((t^(2)))$. The derivative $frac(d y,d t)$ is not explicitly given. At time $t = 2$, the object is at position $(1 \,8)$.

(a) Find the $x$-coordinate of the position of the object at time $t = 4$.

(b) At time $t = 2$, the value of $frac(d y,d t)$ is -7. Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve at the point $(x(2)\, y(2))$.

(c) Find the speed of the object at time $t = 2$.

(d) For $t >= 3$, the line tangent to the curve at $(x(t)\, y(t))$ has a slope of $2 t + 1$. Find the acceleration vector of the object at time $t = 4$.
